items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: He was closer than a brother to me. ... We would call each other Mike. ... I called him Mike.

ctx.x: Did you feel that Buck was like a brother?

Yeah. Yeah. He was closer than a brother to me. I felt he was closer. We could understand each other. We had a whistle that we crossed to each other, know the whistle, you know. It was good. We would call each other Mike. He never called me Bubbles. I never called him Buck. I called him Mike. Oh, we were two, we were two -- I don't think there's any other two negroes in the world like Buck and Bubbles -- no other two, uh-uh,

impossible. Because, first of all, we were so gullible on helpin', helpin' people and doing and loved to do benefits -- hospitals and urban league and all those things -- we loved to do that and we did that along with Bill Robinson. He likes to do benefits, too, he was King Benefit Man. King Benefit of the theatrical profession, he was, Bill Robinson. And I think somebody else -- I think Georgie Jessel was the other one. We handed down, man, when you think about it -- m-m-m. I'm going to do something, I don't…
